title: Rectangular prism
spec: Create a new coordinate system with the Euler angles set to zero degrees for all axes and a translation vector of [0.0, 0.0915, 0.0]. Next, draw a two-dimensional sketch on the first face. Start by creating the first loop, which consists of four lines. Draw the first line from the origin (0.0, 0.0) to (0.0366, 0.0), then draw the second line from (0.0366, 0.0) to (0.0366, 0.6585), followed by the third line from (0.0366, 0.6585) to (0.0, 0.6585), and finally, draw the fourth line from (0.0, 0.6585) back to the origin (0.0, 0.0). After completing the sketch, apply a scale factor of 0.6585 to the entire two-dimensional sketch. Transform the scaled two-dimensional sketch into a three-dimensional object by rotating it using the Euler angles [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] and translating it using the vector [0.0, 0.0915, 0.0]. Finally, extrude the two-dimensional sketch 0.0046 units along the normal direction to create a solid body. The resulting rectangular prism has a length of 0.0366 meters, a width of 0.6585 meters, and a height of 0.0046 meters.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Define the initial sketch
sketch = cq.Workplane("XY").moveTo(0, 0).lineTo(0.0366, 0).lineTo(0.0366, 0.6585).lineTo(0, 0.6585).close()

# Extrude the sketch to create the rectangular prism
extruded = sketch.extrude(0.0046)

# Apply the translation
translated = extruded.translate((0, 0.0915, 0))

# The final model
r = translated

lanes.label: Kimi K3 (high)
lanes.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Flat rectangular bar with chamfered end corners
# Bounding box: X 0.0366, Y 0.6585, Z 0.0046

w = 0.0366 / 2.0   # half width (X)
l = 0.6585 / 2.0   # half length (Y)
c = 0.002          # chamfer size at end corners
t = 0.0046         # thickness (Z)

r = cq.Workplane("XY") \
    .moveTo(-w + c, -l) \
    .lineTo(w - c, -l) \
    .lineTo(w, -l + c) \
    .lineTo(w, l - c) \
    .lineTo(w - c, l) \
    .lineTo(-w + c, l) \
    .lineTo(-w, l - c) \
    .lineTo(-w, -l + c) \
    .close() \
    .extrude(t)
